title: Heads Up: All Garmin Fenix 9 Models $100 Off!
content:
﻿

While Black Friday sales on Garmin Fenix series units are common, it’s virtually unheard of for Garmin to list a sale on a brand-new Fenix unit. I went back through the last few years of Fenix August announcements, and there has not been a Garmin-initiated sale of any just-announced Fenix units during that time. Sure, Uncle Amazon occasionally threw us a brief but appreciated bone, and discounted for a few hours or such, but nothing Garmin-sanctioned.

But here we are, with the first Garmin-approved sale of the Garmin Fenix 9 series, exactly 88 days after the product was announced. I’ll dive into some thoughts on why down below. But, given this rarity, I figured I’d call it out. Of course, the reality is that plenty of other companies discount their products by $100, but equally, the reality is that, around these parts, there’s a ton of interest in the Fenix 9 among DCR readers. Thus, here we are with a quick overview.

(Why this matters/backstory: In the US, companies like Garmin, GoPro, etc., all ‘sanction’ sales, or make allowances under so-called Minimum Advertised Price policies. If you advertise below the MAP price, you’ll get whacked with various penalties, usually including a product turn-off, restricting your ability to refill stock. In the rest of the world, this concept is highly illegal…but hey, it is what it is in the US.)

In any case, here’s what’s on sale, which is basically everything, and what the prices end up at:

Garmin Fenix 9 Base (AMOLED) now $899

Garmin Fenix 9 Pro (AMOLED) now $999

Garmin Fenix 9 Pro (AMOLED) inReach now $1,099

Garmin Fenix 9 Pro Solar (MIP) now $999

Garmin Fenix 9 Pro inReach Solar (MIP) now $1,099

Notably/oddly, the Enduro 4 isn’t seeing a discount here, despite being kinda part of the same family. That said, it only came out last month, so perhaps for Garmin that was a step too far.

In terms of the differences between the models, here’s the gist of it from my review (I’ve got a much longer section detailing them all side-by-side). With the first step, the differences between Base & Pro (non-inReach) are about material finishes/updates (and a bigger storage size that you may or may not care about):

– Pro adds brighter 3,000 nit display (over 2,000 nit on Fenix 9 base)
– Pro adds faster internal processor
– Pro adds full titanium case (vs just the bezel)
– Pro offers a MIP/Solar display option
– Pro adds green flashlight
– Pro gets slightly longer battery life in most categories (due to the processor upgrade)
– Pro 51mm adds 1.5″ screen vs 51mm model is a 1.4″ screen on base

Then the next step up to Pro inReach gets you all the above, plus the below satellite communications & LTE pieces:

– LTE Live two-way voice calls
– LTE LiveTrack (30-second sampling rate)
– LTE Voice Messaging
– LTE Text Messaging
– LTE Weather
– LTE & Satellite Emergency SOS
– LTE Location Check-Ins
– LTE Incident Detection & Assistance
– Satellite Messaging (basic texting)
– Satellite position/location check-ins
– Satellite Emergency SOS (via Garmin Response)
– Satellite updating of weather (new in the Fenix 9 Pro)

What’s my recommendation? Honestly, it just depends on what you want. If you’re gonna leverage the inReach pieces for either LTE or satellite messaging, that makes sense. Of course, keep in mind there’s a subscription fee for that. In terms of base vs Pro, you’re essentially paying for newer/brighter display tech and a new processor. In my review video I show base vs Pro side-by-side in terms of that map-rendering speed. It’s faster, but I wouldn’t call it a dealbreaker. Happy to answer questions down below.

One could speculate why Garmin is putting forth a sale on its flagship wearable. They already had both the Fenix 8 & Fenix 8 Pro on sale, per usual ‘last gen’ sale mantra they usually do. Garmin’s Outdoor segment, which had language in previous quarters, actually turned things around in Q3 (which posted Oct 28th, 2026). I could talk all day about what they probably were thinking when they decided to do this, but according to Garmin’s own earnings statement, they listed new adventure watches as a key reason for the higher revenue (read: the new Fenix 9).

On top of that, we’ve seen a bunch of pricing changes from Garmin in the last 4-6 months that indicate it’s becoming a bit smarter about pricing products at the point where people will still buy them. The Fenix 9 didn’t increase in price over the Fenix 8 Pro, and having an early sale will drive more sales during a period when Garmin is probably seeing a greater slowdown due to the economy.

Of course, there’s also the fact that just a few hours ago COROS teased their Vertix 4 watch, which clearly shows a flashlight on the watch. Many times these companies get their intel from retailers who are briefed on things, and then share it bidirectionally. It wouldn’t at all surprise me if Garmin is aiming to be a spoiler here on price.

Or there’s always the simplest explanation: Garmin is simply (finally) joining everyone else like Apple, Google, GoPro, etc., in putting their newly released devices on sale. Revenue is revenue.

With that – thanks for reading!
